Standardise a long table within samples

Source: R/decostand.R
el_decostand.Rd

Lazy counterparts of the vegan::decostand() methods that need only the non-zero cells. The result is a lazy duckplyr table that can go straight into el_vegdist() or further duckplyr verbs.

Usage

el_decostand(
  x,
  method = c("total", "hellinger", "log", "pa", "rclr"),
  logbase = 2,
  check = TRUE,
  sample = "sample",
  taxon = "taxon",
  quant = "quant"
)

Arguments

x

A data frame or lazy duckplyr table with one row per non-zero sample and taxon. Rows with quant == 0 are dropped.

method

One of the methods above.

logbase

Base of the logarithm for method = "log".

check

If TRUE, run one query to stop on negative, missing or non-finite (NaN, Inf) quantities. Use FALSE to stay entirely lazy.

sample, taxon, quant

Names of the columns in x. The result has only these three columns, with the same names.

Value

A lazy duckplyr table.

Details

  • "total": quantities divided by the sample total.

  • "hellinger": square root of "total".

  • "pa": 1 for every row.

  • "log": log_b(x) + 1 as in vegan. If any value in the whole table is not a whole number, all values are first divided by the smallest positive value of the table, without a warning.

  • "rclr": log(x) minus the mean of log(x) over the sample's rows. This is vegan's "rclr" with impute = FALSE; zeros stay absent where vegan returns NA. See the section on zeros below.

Zeros and rclr

vegan's default, decostand(x, "rclr"), fills the missing cells by matrix completion and then centres rows and columns, which is a global step that changes the non-zero cells too. el_decostand() does not: zero cells stay absent, and a later step that reads absent cells as 0 (such as el_vegdist(method = "euclidean")) puts those taxa at the sample's geometric mean. The result is therefore not vegan's vegdist(method = "robust.aitchison") when the table has zeros; the two agree when it has none.

Examples

library(dplyr)
#> 
#> Attaching package: ‘dplyr’
#> The following objects are masked from ‘package:stats’:
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from ‘package:base’:
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union

# A long table of read counts for 16S ASVs in a time series from the Baltic Sea.
counts <- duckplyr::read_csv_duckdb(
  system.file("extdata", "lmo_free_living.tsv.gz", package = "ecolongr"),
  options = list(delim = "\t", header = TRUE), prudence = "stingy"
)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpBeR5vu/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
metadata <- read.delim(system.file("extdata", "lmo_free_living_samples.tsv", package = "ecolongr"))

# Samples with at least 5,000 reads.
deep <- counts |>
  summarise(reads = sum(quant, na.rm = TRUE), .by = sample) |>
  filter(reads >= 5000) |>
  select(sample)
counts <- semi_join(counts, deep, by = "sample")
metadata <- filter(metadata, sample %in% as.data.frame(deep)$sample)
# A lazy table: nothing is computed until a result is needed.
relative <- counts |> el_decostand("total")
relative |> head() |> as.data.frame()
#>                          sample                            taxon        quant
#> 1 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1017 00a01678e6e0adcd789980f8e123dfc5 3.427626e-05
#> 2 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1017 00db6fe233142d21d2f6c056132b95ed 9.793216e-06
#> 3 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1017 01c25b65bd637c1b1202bc70a73e6d8f 6.365591e-05
#> 4 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1017 01dff5d40f7a902fc54f6b7061676674 3.427626e-05
#> 5 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1017 02af743734992840c4f63515daf859ba 9.793216e-06
#> 6 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1017 02b019aa2218bf9b3d326950c6363127 1.542432e-03

# Standardise, then compute distances.
d <- counts |>
  el_decostand("hellinger") |>
  el_vegdist("euclidean", samples = metadata$sample)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpBeR5vu/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
attr(d, "Size")
#> [1] 335
